title: Chloride-to-sodium ratio offers no clear incremental cross-survey prediction of elevated CRP beyond nonlinear routine chemistry
abstract: We tested whether chloride/sodium improves representation of concurrent CRP>3mg/L beyond separate nonlinear electrolytes, bicarbonate and routine measures. Weighted logistic models trained on 14,402 NHANES III adults were transported unchanged to 4,596 separately recruited NHANES2017–2018 adults. Weighted Brier changed from 0.17111939 to 0.17109964; added-minus-base -0.00001975, approximate fixed-fit target-PSU95% interval [-0.00031895,+0.00022106]. AUC delta was +0.00049082. Joint training-refit/target intervals included zero. No clear incremental prediction was established. This is an exploratory representation test in reused survey cohorts, not equivalence, absence of biological association, sepsis validation or clinical utility.
